hard_deny: Reaching the production database in any way: `railway connect`, `railway run` wrapping mysql/mysqldump, opening a tcp-proxy to the Railway MySQL, `scripts/restore-mysql.sh`, or a Flyway `repair`/`clean`/`migrate` aimed at anything other than the local ./db H2 files. Cloudflare D1 is production data too: `wrangler d1 execute --remote` and the Cloudflare MCP server's `d1_database_query`.

Mutating Railway or Cloudflare infrastructure: `railway up`, `railway config apply`, `railway init`, `railway link`, `railway domain`, `railway variable set|delete`, `wrangler deploy`, deleting a Cloudflare resource with `wrangler r2|kv|d1|queues|hyperdrive|pages ... delete`, or `scripts/bootstrap-deploy.sh` with any stage other than the read-only doctor. The same acts through the Cloudflare MCP server rather than the CLI — any `*_delete` tool — are the same deploy.

Driving the GitHub Actions workflows that ship to Railway and Cloudflare: `gh workflow run|enable|disable`, `gh run rerun|cancel`, `gh release create|delete|edit`, or `gh api` with a mutating method (-X POST|PUT|PATCH|DELETE, or --method). Production deploys from main through Actions, so triggering a workflow is a deploy however it is spelled.
Destroying the repository itself: `gh repo delete`, `gh repo archive`, `gh repo rename`.

Setting, rotating, printing, or copying a production secret or token: `gh secret set|delete`, `gh variable set|delete`, `wrangler secret put|delete|bulk`, `scripts/cf-token.sh`, `scripts/backup-secrets.sh`, `scripts/rotate-admin-password.sh`, or echoing the value of an API key, password, or bearer token.

Reading a credential file with any tool — cat, grep, awk, sed, strings, xxd, base64, cp, rsync — or uploading one: .env, .credentials.json, .netrc, id_rsa, id_ed25519, .pem, .p12, keystores. Piping `env` or `printenv` into curl, wget, or nc is the same act. Read what the code that consumes the file does instead.

Rewriting or deleting shared git history: force-pushing (`--force`, `--force-with-lease`) to any branch on origin, `git push --delete`, or deleting a remote branch or tag. Global options do not change this — `git -C /repo push --force` and `git -c x=y push --force` are the same push.

Disarming the guard: editing, moving, chmod-ing, or deleting anything under ~/.claude/hooks or a project's .claude/hooks, or the settings.json / settings.local.json that register those hooks. The user makes those changes by hand, or relaunches with CLAUDE_GUARD_OFF=1.
soft_deny: Discarding uncommitted work in this repo or a sibling worktree: `git reset --hard`, `git checkout -- .`, `git clean -fd`, `git stash`, `git worktree remove`, or deleting a directory under .claude/worktrees. Finished-but-uncommitted edits have been stranded in worktrees here before, invisible to any branch check — commit first, clean up second.
